about: page 2 $8A00-$8DFF: the behaviour states of the wave 1 probots - for each $1A-byte ALIEN record (U) the routines that enter a state (byte 4 of the record) and the per-frame handlers of the states, which move the probot's position (words 5 and 7 of the record, relative to the player)

P2:8A02.name: probot_do_approach
P2:8A02.desc: per-frame handler of probot state 2 (entry 2 of the handler table P2_8873, also used for a state number past 11): closes in on the player. U = the probot record. makes the position player-relative (P2_8E54), and when both |x| and |y| are under $0300 picks a new behaviour (P2_88A7). otherwise applies P2_8954 and moves x and y a sixteenth of the way towards zero

P2:8A3E.name: probot_go_retreat
P2:8A3E.desc: puts the probot at U in state 3, moving away from the player, and pushes its x and y $10 further from zero so the handler's growth has something to work on. one of the ten entries P2_88A7 picks at random (table P2_888B), and called by P2_88F0 when a probot in player-relative coordinates is within $0200 of the player on both axes

P2:8A5F.name: probot_do_retreat
P2:8A5F.desc: per-frame handler of probot state 3: moves away from the player. U = the probot record. makes the position player-relative, then adds an eighth of x to x and an eighth of y to y. when |x| or |y| has reached $4000, or an addition overflows, it picks a new behaviour (P2_88A7) instead

P2:8A9D.name: probot_go_leave
P2:8A9D.desc: puts the probot at U in state 11, leaving the field, and pushes its x and y $10 further from zero. not called directly: P2_88A7 loads its address and calls it through JSR ,X when w1_spawn is minus, which the end of the wave sets

P2:8ABE.name: probot_do_leave
P2:8ABE.desc: per-frame handler of probot state 11: the probot flies off at the end of the wave. U = the probot record. makes the position player-relative and adds an eighth of x and y to themselves each frame, as the state 3 handler does. when |x| or |y| reaches $7800, or an addition overflows, it frees the record by clearing bytes 0 and 1

P2:8B07.name: probot_go_drift
P2:8B07.desc: puts the probot at U in state 5 and gives it a random velocity in words $15 and $17 of the record: two random words multiplied (matrix program MS_PERS) by twice the sum of the high bytes of |x| and |y|, at least $0100, so a distant probot gets a larger one. one of the ten entries P2_88A7 picks at random

P2:8B4B.name: probot_do_drift
P2:8B4B.desc: per-frame handler of probot state 5: moves by the velocity in words $15 and $17 of the record. U = the probot record. while the probot is in view (bit $10 of byte 1) the velocity loses a thirty-second each frame and P2_8954 is applied. then the velocity is added to x and y, and a velocity component that points outwards while its coordinate is past +$4000 or -$4000 is negated, so the probot turns back

P2:8BD4.name: probot_go_point
P2:8BD4.desc: puts the probot at U in state 6 and picks the point it flies to, kept player-relative in words $15 and $17 of the record: on each axis a random distance of up to $1FE0 plus $0200 plus the player's height s1_tz, with a random sign. one of the ten entries P2_88A7 picks at random. P2_8CD6 is the same code for state 7

P2:8C14.name: probot_go_ahead
P2:8C14.desc: puts the probot at U in state 9 and picks the point it flies to: a scratch block point with x a random distance ($0200 plus the player's height plus up to $1FE0), y a random part of that distance with a random sign, and z 0 goes through matrix program $60, and the result less the player's position ($5098, s1_ty) is stored in words $15 and $17 of the record. P2_88A7 calls it for a probot that is not in view and not already in state 9, as one of its ten random entries, and by w1_level in the last $96 counts of the phase timer

P2:8C62.name: probot_do_seek
P2:8C62.desc: per-frame handler of probot states 6 and 9: flies to the point in words $15 and $17 of the record. U = the probot record. applies P2_898D to the point, then moves x and y by a sixteenth of the distance left, a step that is halved until it is within +-$0400. when the probot is within $0200 of the point on both axes it picks a new behaviour (P2_88A7)

P2:8CD6.name: probot_go_point2
P2:8CD6.desc: puts the probot at U in state 7 and picks the point it flies to, in words $15 and $17 of the record. the same code as P2_8BD4 but for the state number: a random distance of up to $1FE0 plus $0200 plus the player's height on each axis, with a random sign. one of the ten entries P2_88A7 picks at random

P2:8D16.name: probot_do_seek2
P2:8D16.desc: per-frame handler of probot state 7: flies to the point in words $15 and $17 of the record. the same as the handler of states 6 and 9 (P2_8C62) except that a step past +-$0400 is cut to $0400 or -$0400 and not halved. when the probot is within $0200 of the point on both axes it picks a new behaviour (P2_88A7)

P2:8D86.name: probot_go_circle
P2:8D86.desc: puts the probot at U in state 8 and stores a random turn rate in word $15 of the record: $0100 to $03FD, positive or negative by the sign of RND_S3. one of the ten entries P2_88A7 picks at random, and one of the four it picks by w1_level in the last $96 counts of the phase timer

P2:8DA8.name: probot_do_circle
P2:8DA8.desc: per-frame handler of probot state 8: circles the player. U = the probot record. applies P2_8954, then multiplies x and y by the turn rate in word $15 of the record (matrix program MS_PERS) and takes the y product off x and adds the x product to y, a small rotation of the player-relative position about the player. it never picks a new behaviour itself: P2_88F0 does that at random

P2:8DD2.name: probot_go_orbit
P2:8DD2.desc: puts the probot at U in state 10 and picks the point its handler (P2_8E1D) turns it around, in words $15 and $17 of the record: $0400 to one side of the probot on one axis, side and axis random, and a random -$0400 to +$03F8 from it on the other axis. one of the ten entries P2_88A7 picks at random, and one of the four it picks by w1_level in the last $96 counts of the phase timer

comments.P2:8DE2: sign of RND_S1 decides the side
comments.P2:8DEB: sign of RND_S2 decides the axis

4855.name: rnd_s4
4855.desc: fourth saved random byte, the byte after RND_S3: rnd_set stores the old RND_S1/RND_S2 pair as a word at RND_S3, so the old RND_S2 lands here. page 2 uses it as one more random byte when it picks a probot's behaviour and target point

5098.name: s1_tx
5098.desc: MS_TX+M_S1: the player's universe x position, word, first of the position words $5098/s1_ty/s1_tz. the pages add it to and take it off an object's x to change between universe and player-relative coordinates

questions: P2:8C4A - matrix program $60 has two names in the defines (MS_PSUB, presub, and MS_S1UN, S1 view to universe). here the code takes the player's position off the result, which fits a conversion from the player's view to universe coordinates (a point ahead of the player, random distance and sideways offset), but I did not verify what the program does with block MS_X0BC, so the description only says what goes in and out

P2:8A22 etc - P2_8954 and P2_898D (outside this range) multiply s1_vx and s1_vy by (|x|+|y|)/4 of the probot's position and take the products off the position or off the target point. the descriptions here just say they are applied

record layout as used here, for whoever names the fields: byte 0 bit $08 = position is in universe coordinates (P2_8E54 clears it and makes the position player-relative), byte 1 bit $10 = in view this frame (set by P2_8FD3), byte 4 = behaviour state 0-11, words 5 and 7 = x and y, words $15 and $17 = per-state data: velocity in state 5, target point in states 6, 7 and 9, turn rate (word $15 only) in state 8, centre point in state 10
P2:8C41 - the carried comment TOP OF SIDE PANELS is the Star Wars line L884A (STD M_Z0 before MS_PSB2) and means nothing here, dropped and replaced

states by handler table P2_8873 (outside this range): 0 P2_89D2 idle, 1 P2_89DB, 2 approach, 3 retreat, 4 P2_89F0, 5 drift, 6 and 9 fly to point (halving step), 7 fly to point (clamped step), 8 circle the player, 10 P2_8E1D turn around a point, 11 leave. the tables P2_888B (ten random state entries) and P2_889F (four entries by w1_level and 3) hold the go_ routines
